## GPU Communication

## NVLink and RDMA Domains

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="imgs/img_in_image_box_187_307_1794_1197.jpg" alt="Image" width="80%" /></div>


· NVLink connects local GPU peers; RDMA connects GPU memory through NICs.

The throughput path composes these domains instead of treating every hop alike.

<!-- page: 5 -->

• The NIC reads or writes registered GPU memory without a host-memory staging copy.

• Direct data movement still requires setup, valid memory mappings, and synchronization.

## Low-Latency Dispatch

## Reserving Slots with Atomics

A partition belongs to one source rank.

slot = atomicAdd(&reserve[e], 1);
peer = e / 9;
local_e = e % 9;
put_nbi(remote[local_e][rank][slot],
staged_token, peer);

Each concurrent sender receives a different slot.

• One atomic increment allocates a unique slot among local sends to the same expert.

Source-rank slices separate GPUs; the atomic separates concurrent warps on one GPU.

n = -flag - 1;

## Publishing Readiness to the Receiver

Sender GPU

Ordered peer / QP


<table border=1 style='margin: auto; word-wrap: break-word;'><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'></td></tr></table>

post payload WRITEs
publish local issued progress
wait until local requests are issued
post count AMO: -(n + 1)

n = 0 still publishes -1, so the receiver can finish waiting.

· The local finish counter records issued sends, not remote payload completion.

- A count AMO follows payload writes on the same QP; encode n tokens as -(n + 1).

## RDMA-to-NVLink Forwarding

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="imgs/img_in_image_box_109_375_1902_1034.jpg" alt="Image" width="89%" /></div>


Same token  $ \rightarrow $ one remote node  $ \rightarrow $ several final GPU ranks

· RDMA connects the same local GPU index across nodes; NVLink reaches the final local ranks.

· A token crosses RDMA once per destination node, then its rank mask drives local forwarding.
